overall: Los Angeles is experiencing a classic marine-layer June Gloom pattern on June 25, with mostly cloudy skies, patchy fog, and onshore southwest flow keeping temperatures suppressed. As of 11:45 ET (8:45 AM PDT), the running max is only 64.9°F with essentially flat velocity (+0.0°F/hr), though the 2-hour trend shows a modest +0.9°F/hr warming rate. Active south-southwest swell and coastal hazard alerts for adjacent SoCal counties reinforce the deep marine influence.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show meaningful spread: ECMWF at 68.4°F and NBM at 67.0°F cluster near the NWS official high of 69°F, while HRRR runs notably warmer at 71.1°F. The current running max of 64.9°F is tracking below all model guidance at this hour, but the predicted peak is still roughly 5 hours away (NWP models peg the peak near 16–17h ET / 1–2 PM PDT), so early-morning underperformance does not yet rule out an afternoon recovery if the marine layer partially erodes.
max_temp_prediction: The balance of evidence points to a final TMAX in the 69–71°F range. The NWS official call of 69°F and the ECMWF/NBM cluster around 68–68.5°F anchor the lower end, while HRRR and the META model (peak probability 27.1% in the 70–71°F bucket, with the distribution skewed toward 72–75°F) suggest modest upside if afternoon clearing occurs. Negative acceleration (-0.9°F/hr²) and persistent cloud cover are the primary headwinds; confidence is moderate given the wide model spread and the strong marine layer already in place. The ensemble model signals both flag a skip/avoid recommendation, reinforcing genuine uncertainty rather than a high-conviction setup.
